chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Khalid, from Al-Jamourani, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Amr ibn Jubayr Al-Azrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband upon the woman?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'There are many more than that.' She said, 'So inform me about something from it.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'It is not for her to fast except with his permission, meaning voluntary fasting, and she should not leave her house except with his permission, and it is upon her to perfume herself with the best of her perfume, and wear the best of her clothes, and adorn herself with the best of her adornments, and present herself to him morning and evening, and much more than that are his rights upon her.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific rights of a husband upon his wife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the wife's duties of 'tamkin' (physical availability) and 'nushuz' prevention, reflecting the classical Shia juristic view of marital harmony through mutual rights. It underscores the spiritual and social dimensions of marriage, where the wife’s adornment and readiness are seen as acts of devotion and fulfillment of conjugal rights.
